BARFLR.overview: BARFLR is a 2D calibration curve that applies an altitude-dependent barometric pressure correction to the deceleration control manifold pressure calculation. At higher altitudes, atmospheric pressure is substantially lower than at sea level. Because manifold absolute pressure is measured relative to absolute vacuum, closed-throttle overrun at high elevation produces much lower absolute MAP readings than at sea level. Without barometric compensation, the calculated decel control MAP would become misaligned with actual intake manifold pressure, either causing false dashpot opening steps or inadequate deceleration cushioning. BARFLR provides a barometric trim adder to keep the decel control MAP threshold properly calibrated across varying altitudes. In factory calibrations, BARFLR is configured as a single baseline point that maintains zero offset under standard atmospheric pressure.

Without barometric compensation, the calculated decel control MAP would become misaligned with actual intake manifold pressure, either causing false dashpot opening steps or inadequate deceleration cushioning. `BARFLR` provides a barometric trim adder to keep the decel control MAP threshold properly calibrated across varying altitudes. In factory calibrations, `BARFLR` is configured as a single baseline point that maintains zero offset under standard atmospheric pressure.
BARFLR.tuners_guide: BARFLR rarely requires modification unless tuning a vehicle specifically for extreme high-altitude operation (such as Pikes Peak hill climbs or high mountain passes). If an engine decelerates smoothly at sea level but suffers from severe decel hanging or floating idle when driven at high elevations, reducing the barometric correction in BARFLR will lower the decel control MAP threshold to align with thin mountain air. For standard sea-level and moderate-altitude street driving, retain the factory table point.

* **High-Altitude Decel Hang**: * If decel idle floats or hangs only at high elevations, trim `BARFLR` downward to lower the control MAP threshold in thin air.
* **Sea-Level Baseline**: * Retain factory setting (0 offset) for normal sea-level and moderate elevation environments.
* **Companion Verification**: * Works in parallel with `BARAIS`, which adjusts idle stepper motor opening steps for barometric pressure.

DCLRFQ.overview: DCLRFQ defines the minimum time delay that must elapse between successive stepper motor repositioning pulses during deceleration dashpot control. When the vehicle decelerates with closed throttle, manifold pressure drops rapidly, triggering the decel dashpot routines to open the stepper motor to catch the descent. If the controller were permitted to command stepper movements on every single program loop execution, the stepper motor would outpace its mechanical response capabilities, dropping pulses and becoming physically desynchronized. DCLRFQ acts as a pacing filter, enforcing a minimum settling delay between decel stepper motor movements. In factory calibrations, DCLRFQ is set to 63 counts, enforcing a settling interval of approximately 700 milliseconds between decel stepper pulses.
DCLRFQ.overview_markdown: `DCLRFQ` defines the minimum time delay that must elapse between successive stepper motor repositioning pulses during deceleration dashpot control. When the vehicle decelerates with closed throttle, manifold pressure drops rapidly, triggering the decel dashpot routines to open the stepper motor to catch the descent. If the controller were permitted to command stepper movements on every single program loop execution, the stepper motor would outpace its mechanical response capabilities, dropping pulses and becoming physically desynchronized. `DCLRFQ` acts as a pacing filter, enforcing a minimum settling delay between decel stepper motor movements. In factory calibrations, `DCLRFQ` is set to 63 counts, enforcing a settling interval of approximately 700 milliseconds between decel stepper pulses.
DCLRFQ.tuners_guide: DCLRFQ controls how rapidly the idle stepper motor can respond to fast deceleration transients. If your vehicle suffers from sudden stalling when you let off the throttle quickly, lowering DCLRFQ to 35 to 45 counts (~400 to 500 ms) allows the controller to pulse the stepper motor open more frequently, catching rapid RPM drops. This adjustment is particularly valuable on engines with lightweight flywheels or race clutches where engine speed plunges faster than factory calibration expects. Never set DCLRFQ below 20 counts (~220 ms), as the mechanical stepper motor cannot complete its physical steps that quickly, leading to lost steps and inaccurate motor positioning.
DCLRFQ.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Catching Rapid Decel Plunges**: * Lower `DCLRFQ` from 63 to 35 to 45 counts on cars with lightweight flywheels to allow faster stepper motor intervention on throttle snap-shut.
* **Preventing Motor Desynchronization**: * Do not lower `DCLRFQ` below 20 counts, as pulsing the coils faster than the motor pintle can move will cause skipped steps.
* **Factory Pacing**: * Factory setting of 63 counts (~700 ms) provides conservative, reliable stepper motor tracking on standard rotating assemblies.

DATHOT.overview: DATHOT defines the minimum engine coolant temperature threshold required before the controller enables adaptive idle airflow calibration. While an engine is warming up, internal friction changes continuously and auxiliary warm-up airflow tables are actively propping the idle stepper open. Attempting to learn long-term baseline idle airflow characteristics while the engine is cold would severely skew the learned trim once the engine reaches full operating temperature. DATHOT locks out adaptive idle airflow learning until the engine reaches full thermal maturity. In factory calibrations, DATHOT is set to 205 counts, corresponding to a coolant temperature threshold of 175 °F.
DATHOT.overview_markdown: `DATHOT` defines the minimum engine coolant temperature threshold required before the controller enables adaptive idle airflow calibration. While an engine is warming up, internal friction changes continuously and auxiliary warm-up airflow tables are actively propping the idle stepper open. Attempting to learn long-term baseline idle airflow characteristics while the engine is cold would severely skew the learned trim once the engine reaches full operating temperature. `DATHOT` locks out adaptive idle airflow learning until the engine reaches full thermal maturity. In factory calibrations, `DATHOT` is set to 205 counts, corresponding to a coolant temperature threshold of 175 °F.
DATHOT.tuners_guide: DATHOT should match your engine thermostat rating. If you install a low-temperature 160 °F thermostat, the engine may operate between 165 °F and 172 °F during cold weather driving. Under these conditions, coolant temperature will never cross the factory 175 °F threshold in DATHOT, completely preventing adaptive idle airflow learning from ever taking place. When running a 160 °F thermostat, lower DATHOT to 155 °F or 160 °F (180 to 190 counts) so that adaptive idle trim functions normally. Never lower DATHOT below 140 °F, as cold engine friction will distort the learned baseline.
DATHOT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Thermostat Rating Alignment**: * If running a 160 °F or 170 °F thermostat, lower `DATHOT` to 155 °F to 160 °F so adaptive idle airflow learning can activate during normal cruising.
* **Preventing Cold Trim Distortion**: * Keep `DATHOT` at or above 150 °F to ensure the engine is fully warmed up before the ECU adapts its base idle air calibration.
* **Stock 180 °F Thermostats**: * Retain factory setting of 175 °F (205 counts) when using standard 180 °F or 195 °F thermostats.

DADRPM.overview: DADRPM defines the engine speed error deadband window within which adaptive idle airflow learning is permitted to operate. If engine speed is significantly above or below target idle, the engine is experiencing a transient disturbance (such as an accessory load engaging or disengaging) rather than reflecting true steady-state mechanical airflow needs. Allowing adaptive learning to adjust idle trim during an RPM disturbance would skew the learned calibration in the wrong direction. DADRPM enforces an RPM stability window: only when actual engine speed is within DADRPM of target idle speed will the controller adjust the adaptive trim integrator. In factory calibrations, DADRPM is set to 4 counts, representing an RPM deadband window of 32 RPM.
DADRPM.overview_markdown: `DADRPM` defines the engine speed error deadband window within which adaptive idle airflow learning is permitted to operate. If engine speed is significantly above or below target idle, the engine is experiencing a transient disturbance (such as an accessory load engaging or disengaging) rather than reflecting true steady-state mechanical airflow needs. Allowing adaptive learning to adjust idle trim during an RPM disturbance would skew the learned calibration in the wrong direction. `DADRPM` enforces an RPM stability window: only when actual engine speed is within `DADRPM` of target idle speed will the controller adjust the adaptive trim integrator. In factory calibrations, `DADRPM` is set to 4 counts, representing an RPM deadband window of 32 RPM.
DADRPM.tuners_guide: DADRPM must be adapted when installing high-performance camshafts. Factory engines idle smoothly with very little RPM fluctuation, allowing a tight 32 RPM deadband. However, aggressive aftermarket camshafts with considerable valve overlap naturally produce a choppy, lopey idle profile where engine speed fluctuates by 40 to 60 RPM around the target setpoint even under perfect operating conditions. With a tight 32 RPM window, the choppy idle will constantly breach DADRPM, causing adaptive idle airflow learning to be suspended indefinitely. Widening DADRPM to 8 to 12 counts (64 to 96 RPM) allows adaptive idle learning to function properly on camshafts with aggressive lope.
DADRPM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Lumpy Camshaft Idle Accommodation**: * Increase `DADRPM` to 8 to 12 counts (64 to 96 RPM) on engines with significant valve overlap to allow adaptive learning to tolerate normal lope dither.
* **Stock Camshaft Tightness**: * Retain factory 4 counts (32 RPM) on smooth-idling stock or mild street camshafts.
* **Excessive Window Warning**: * Do not widen `DADRPM` beyond 16 counts (128 RPM), as the ECU may mistake an active idle flare or sag for a stable idle condition.

DAACF.overview: DAACF defines the additional manifold pressure offset added to the deceleration control calculation whenever the air conditioning compressor clutch is engaged. When the air conditioner is running, the mechanical compressor pump imposes a continuous parasitic torque load on the engine crankshaft. If the driver lifts off the throttle abruptly with the A/C clutch engaged, this additional parasitic drag causes engine speed to fall much more rapidly than normal, increasing the likelihood of an undershoot stall. DAACF elevates the calculated decel control manifold pressure whenever the A/C clutch is active, which commands extra opening steps from DAISOP during throttle lift-off to cushion the compressor load. In factory calibrations, DAACF is set to 18 counts (approximately 2.1 psi absolute / 4.2 inHg), providing a dedicated decel dashpot buffer for air conditioning operation.
DAACF.overview_markdown: `DAACF` defines the additional manifold pressure offset added to the deceleration control calculation whenever the air conditioning compressor clutch is engaged. When the air conditioner is running, the mechanical compressor pump imposes a continuous parasitic torque load on the engine crankshaft. If the driver lifts off the throttle abruptly with the A/C clutch engaged, this additional parasitic drag causes engine speed to fall much more rapidly than normal, increasing the likelihood of an undershoot stall. `DAACF` elevates the calculated decel control manifold pressure whenever the A/C clutch is active, which commands extra opening steps from `DAISOP` during throttle lift-off to cushion the compressor load. In factory calibrations, `DAACF` is set to 18 counts (approximately 2.1 psi absolute / 4.2 inHg), providing a dedicated decel dashpot buffer for air conditioning operation.
DAACF.tuners_guide: DAACF is the primary adjustment for preventing deceleration stalls that occur exclusively when the air conditioning is running. If your vehicle decelerates smoothly with the air conditioner off, but dips severely below idle or stalls when you push the clutch in or let off the gas with the A/C on, increase DAACF by 4 to 8 counts (up to 22 to 26 counts). This will command a larger stepper motor dashpot opening during A/C deceleration, neutralizing compressor drag. Do not raise DAACF excessively, as this can cause engine speed to hang high when decelerating with the air conditioning active.
DAACF.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Curing A/C Decel Stalls**: * Increase `DAACF` from 18 to 22 to 26 counts if the engine stalls on throttle lift-off only when the air conditioning is engaged.
* **Eliminating A/C Decel Hang**: * If engine speed refuses to come down cleanly when decelerating with the A/C on, reduce `DAACF` slightly.
* **Parasitic Drag Compensation**: * Directly counteracts compressor torque absorption on the crankshaft during closed-throttle overrun.

Takes effect during idle air calculation, applying an airflow factor delta when the air conditioning compressor is running.

DANOM.overview: DANOM defines the base nominal calibration offset utilized by the Chrysler SBEC deceleration airflow calculation. To provide smooth throttle dashpot cushioning without holding engine speed artificially high, the SBEC calculates a synthetic decel control manifold absolute pressure threshold. This calculated threshold represents the expected intake manifold vacuum curve during closed-throttle overrun. DANOM serves as the foundational base term to which the learned adaptive airflow integrator is added, followed by coolant temperature, run time, and air conditioning offsets. In factory calibrations, DANOM is set to 18 counts (approximately 2.1 psi absolute / 4.2 inHg), providing an initial manifold pressure baseline for decel dashpot air calculations.
DANOM.overview_markdown: `DANOM` defines the base nominal calibration offset utilized by the Chrysler SBEC deceleration airflow calculation. To provide smooth throttle dashpot cushioning without holding engine speed artificially high, the SBEC calculates a synthetic decel control manifold absolute pressure threshold. This calculated threshold represents the expected intake manifold vacuum curve during closed-throttle overrun. `DANOM` serves as the foundational base term to which the learned adaptive airflow integrator is added, followed by coolant temperature, run time, and air conditioning offsets. In factory calibrations, `DANOM` is set to 18 counts (approximately 2.1 psi absolute / 4.2 inHg), providing an initial manifold pressure baseline for decel dashpot air calculations.
DANOM.tuners_guide: DANOM directly establishes the baseline sensitivity of the deceleration dashpot system. Raising DANOM shifts the calculated decel control manifold pressure higher, which causes the controller to perceive a larger vacuum delta when the throttle snaps shut, commanding more aggressive opening steps from DAISOP to cushion deceleration. This is particularly effective for eliminating stall-on-decel on vehicles with lightweight flywheels or aggressive performance camshafts. However, if DANOM is increased too high, deceleration manifold pressure will persistently exceed actual manifold pressure, causing the engine to hang at elevated RPM or float during gear changes. Lowering DANOM reduces decel airflow, producing sharper engine braking upon lift-off.
DANOM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Curing Deceleration Stalls**: * Increase `DANOM` from 18 to 22 to 26 counts if the engine tends to dip below idle and stall when releasing the throttle abruptly.
* **Lightweight Rotating Assemblies**: * Raising `DANOM` provides a stronger electronic dashpot cushion to catch engines with lightened flywheels that lose momentum rapidly.
* **Eliminating High-RPM Decel Hang**: * If engine speed refuses to drop cleanly when coasting, lower `DANOM` to reduce the baseline decel control threshold.
DANOM.operating_conditions:
Takes effect during idle air calculation, defining the nominal baseline airflow step position for idle regulation.

DCALTM.overview: DCALTM defines the post-start time delay that must elapse before the engine controller is permitted to begin adaptive idle airflow calibration. Immediately following engine start, combustion dynamics, cylinder wall temperature, and manifold pressure undergo rapid transient changes as the engine stabilizes. If the adaptive learning routines were allowed to integrate intake manifold pressure during this settling period, transient post-start vacuum instability would corrupt the long-term learned idle airflow trim. DCALTM enforces a mandatory run-time delay before the DACAL adaptive integrator is unlocked. In factory calibrations, DCALTM is set to 25 counts, enforcing a post-start stabilization period of approximately 1.6 seconds.
DCALTM.overview_markdown: `DCALTM` defines the post-start time delay that must elapse before the engine controller is permitted to begin adaptive idle airflow calibration. Immediately following engine start, combustion dynamics, cylinder wall temperature, and manifold pressure undergo rapid transient changes as the engine stabilizes. If the adaptive learning routines were allowed to integrate intake manifold pressure during this settling period, transient post-start vacuum instability would corrupt the long-term learned idle airflow trim. `DCALTM` enforces a mandatory run-time delay before the DACAL adaptive integrator is unlocked. In factory calibrations, `DCALTM` is set to 25 counts, enforcing a post-start stabilization period of approximately 1.6 seconds.
DCALTM.tuners_guide: DCALTM prevents premature adaptive idle air learning. On modified engines with large injectors or aggressive camshafts that take several seconds to clear out cranking fuel and establish a steady idle vacuum, increasing DCALTM to 5 to 10 seconds (80 to 160 counts) ensures the adaptive integrator does not learn false airflow errors during rough post-start idling. Lowering DCALTM allows adaptive learning to begin sooner, but setting it below 1.0 second risks corrupting learned idle trim during cold cranking flare.
DCALTM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Preventing Post-Start Trim Corruption**: * Increase `DCALTM` to 5.0 to 10.0 seconds on modified engines with long post-start stabilization periods to prevent the ECU from learning inaccurate idle trim.
* **Factory Baseline**: * Factory setting of 25 counts (~1.6 seconds) is suitable for stock and mild street setups.
* **Low Setting Hazard**: * Setting `DCALTM` too low allows cranking vacuum dips to skew the long-term idle airflow baseline.

DCALRT.overview: DCALRT defines the loop counter bitmask that paces the execution frequency of the DACAL adaptive idle airflow integrator. Adaptive idle air learning compensates for long-term mechanical changes in the engine, such as throttle body carbon buildup, PCV valve wear, or minor vacuum leaks. Because these physical changes occur very slowly over weeks and months, the adaptive learning integrator must update at an extremely deliberate pace so that temporary intake manifold pressure fluctuations are ignored. DCALRT masks the main program loop counter to enforce a slow learning rate. In factory calibrations, DCALRT is set to 127 counts, representing a binary bitmask allowing the integrator to adjust only once every 128 main loop passes, or approximately every 1.4 seconds.
DCALRT.overview_markdown: `DCALRT` defines the loop counter bitmask that paces the execution frequency of the DACAL adaptive idle airflow integrator. Adaptive idle air learning compensates for long-term mechanical changes in the engine, such as throttle body carbon buildup, PCV valve wear, or minor vacuum leaks. Because these physical changes occur very slowly over weeks and months, the adaptive learning integrator must update at an extremely deliberate pace so that temporary intake manifold pressure fluctuations are ignored. `DCALRT` masks the main program loop counter to enforce a slow learning rate. In factory calibrations, `DCALRT` is set to 127 counts, representing a binary bitmask allowing the integrator to adjust only once every 128 main loop passes, or approximately every 1.4 seconds.
DCALRT.tuners_guide: DCALRT controls the integration speed of the adaptive idle airflow trim. The factory setting of 127 counts (every 128th loop) provides excellent long-term stability and should be retained for street applications. If you are actively calibrating a newly built engine on an engine dyno or chassis dyno and want to observe adaptive trim adapt quickly, lowering DCALRT to 31 (every 32nd loop) or 15 (every 16th loop) accelerates the learning process. Always return DCALRT to 127 counts before delivering the vehicle for road driving, as fast adaptive learning can chase transient manifold pressure dips and cause surging.
DCALRT.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Dyno Tuning & Fast Learning**: * Temporarily lower `DCALRT` to 31 or 15 counts during dyno calibration to accelerate adaptive airflow learning.
* **Street Stability**: * Retain factory setting of 127 counts (every 128th loop) for normal driving to ensure long-term stability and filter out short-term vacuum perturbations.
* **Mask Formatting**: * Must be configured as a power-of-two minus one value (15, 31, 63, 127, 255).

DCLMIN.overview: DCLMIN establishes a minimum lower clamp on the calculated deceleration control manifold absolute pressure value. During closed-throttle deceleration, intake manifold vacuum reaches extreme levels. If the synthetic decel control MAP calculation were allowed to drop to near-absolute zero pressure, the difference between actual MAP and control MAP would become artificially small, preventing the controller from recognizing deep deceleration vacuum and failing to open the dashpot. DCLMIN enforces a hard lower floor on the calculated decel control MAP. In factory calibrations, DCLMIN is set to 10 counts, enforcing an absolute pressure floor of approximately 1.1 psi absolute (2.3 inHg / 27.6 inHg vacuum).
DCLMIN.overview_markdown: `DCLMIN` establishes a minimum lower clamp on the calculated deceleration control manifold absolute pressure value. During closed-throttle deceleration, intake manifold vacuum reaches extreme levels. If the synthetic decel control MAP calculation were allowed to drop to near-absolute zero pressure, the difference between actual MAP and control MAP would become artificially small, preventing the controller from recognizing deep deceleration vacuum and failing to open the dashpot. `DCLMIN` enforces a hard lower floor on the calculated decel control MAP. In factory calibrations, `DCLMIN` is set to 10 counts, enforcing an absolute pressure floor of approximately 1.1 psi absolute (2.3 inHg / 27.6 inHg vacuum).
DCLMIN.tuners_guide: DCLMIN ensures that the deceleration dashpot calculation always maintains positive opening authority under deep overrun vacuum. Raising DCLMIN to 14 to 18 counts (1.6 to 2.1 psi absolute) elevates the minimum control MAP floor, ensuring that when the throttle snaps shut from high RPM, a larger pressure delta is generated, commanding more opening steps from DAISOP. This provides extra anti-stall protection on engines with very tight ring seals or high compression that pull exceptionally deep deceleration vacuum. Do not raise DCLMIN above 25 counts, as this can cause the controller to mistake light part-throttle cruising for a decel condition.
DCLMIN.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Deep Overrun Anti-Stall**: * Increase `DCLMIN` to 14 to 18 counts if the engine pulls extreme overrun vacuum and stalls when the clutch is pressed.
* **Factory Minimum Baseline**: * Factory setting of 10 counts (~1.1 psi absolute) guarantees a safe floor on stock induction systems.
* **Part-Throttle Boundary**: * Keep `DCLMIN` below 25 counts to prevent false decel triggering during light part-throttle cruising.
DCLMIN.operating_conditions:
Takes effect during closed-throttle deceleration, intake manifold vacuum reaches extreme levels.

DCLMIN.raw_text: DCLMIN establishes a minimum lower clamp on the calculated deceleration control manifold absolute pressure value. During closed-throttle deceleration, intake manifold vacuum reaches extreme levels. DCLMN2.overview: DCLMN2 defines the master safety manifold absolute pressure lockout threshold below which all deceleration idle stepper motor control and air conditioning kick routines are inhibited. Under conditions of extreme closed-throttle engine overrun from high RPM (such as downhill engine braking), intake manifold absolute pressure can plummet to near total vacuum. At these extreme vacuum levels, erratic pressure transients can occur, and attempting to actuate the idle stepper motor or engage A/C kicks can cause unexpected engine flare or motor hunting. If both actual manifold pressure and calculated control manifold pressure are below DCLMN2, all stepper motor manipulation is completely suspended. In factory calibrations, DCLMN2 is set to 13 counts, corresponding to an absolute pressure lockout threshold of approximately 1.5 psi absolute (3.0 inHg / 26.9 inHg vacuum).

DCLMN2.tuners_guide: DCLMN2 functions as a critical stability lockout during severe engine overrun. In almost all performance applications, DCLMN2 should remain at its factory calibration of 13 counts (~1.5 psi absolute). If DCLMN2 is set too high (for example, above 25 counts), the controller will prematurely lock out decel dashpot operation during normal around-town deceleration, causing the engine to drop into a sudden stall before the stepper motor can intervene. If set to zero, the safety lockout is effectively disabled, which can allow anomalous stepper motor dithering during extreme downhill engine braking.

* **Premature Lockout Hazard**: * Do not raise `DCLMN2` above 20 counts, as this will disable dashpot control during normal deceleration, causing frequent stalls.
* **Multi-Routine Enforcement**: * Enforces identical safety lockouts across both the decel dashpot routines and the A/C clutch transition routines.

DLYTIM.overview: DLYTIM defines the time delay that the engine controller holds the idle air stepper motor in its open dashpot position after the throttle snaps shut while the vehicle is moving. When the driver releases the accelerator pedal while driving at road speed, holding the idle air valve open momentarily cushions engine deceleration, smooths the transition into closed-throttle overrun, and prevents sudden driveline snatch. Whenever closed throttle is detected and vehicle speed is above the rolling switch point set in MPHREF, the controller reloads the feedback lockout timer with DLYTIM. In factory calibrations, DLYTIM is set to 18 counts, enforcing an open dashpot hold delay of approximately 1.1 seconds while moving.

DLYTIM.tuners_guide: DLYTIM governs deceleration manners and shift smoothness while driving. If your vehicle experiences harsh driveline bucking or jerks aggressively when lifting off the throttle during high-speed cruising, increasing DLYTIM to 1.5 or 2.0 seconds (24 to 32 counts) prolongs the dashpot air hold, smoothing out the deceleration transient. However, setting DLYTIM too high causes the engine to hang onto RPM during upshifts, making gear changes feel sluggish or causing the car to continue pushing forward when trying to engine brake. Lowering DLYTIM to 0.5 to 0.8 seconds provides more immediate engine vacuum braking upon throttle release.
DLYTIM.tuners_guide_markdown:

* **Enhancing Engine Braking**: * Lower `DLYTIM` to 0.5 to 0.8 seconds if you prefer sharper, immediate engine vacuum braking on throttle lift.
* **Preventing Shift Hang**: * Setting `DLYTIM` excessively high makes RPM linger between gear shifts on manual transmission vehicles.

DLYTIM2.overview: DLYTIM2 defines the time delay that the engine controller holds the idle air stepper motor in open dashpot position after the throttle snaps shut while the vehicle is stopped or moving at low speed with engine RPM below DLYRPM. DLYTM3.overview: DLYTM3 defines the extended time delay that the engine controller holds the idle air stepper motor in open dashpot position when the throttle snaps shut at a standstill with engine speed above DLYRPM. When an engine is revved up to high RPM in neutral and the throttle is abruptly released, the rotating assembly generates massive momentum, and intake manifold vacuum plunges violently. To safely catch the engine from high RPM without risking a severe vacuum undershoot stall, the controller enforces an extended dashpot delay before allowing closed-loop idle feedback to take over. Whenever closed throttle is detected at low vehicle speed (below MPHREF) and engine speed is at or above DLYRPM, the controller loads DLYTM3 into the feedback lockout timer. In factory calibrations, DLYTM3 is set to 255 counts, providing a prolonged dashpot hold of approximately 16 seconds until engine speed settles safely.

DLYTM3.tuners_guide: DLYTM3 governs high-RPM neutral throttle release behavior. The factory setting of 255 counts (maximum timer saturation, ~16 seconds) is very conservative, ensuring that revving in neutral will never result in an undershoot stall. However, on high-performance manual transmission vehicles, this maximum setting can make the engine linger at an elevated idle for an excessively long time after revving in neutral. Lowering DLYTM3 to 3.0 to 5.0 seconds (48 to 80 counts) allows engine speed to drop back to base idle much more crisply after revving the engine, giving the car a more responsive, race-like throttle return. Do not lower DLYTM3 below 2.0 seconds, or the engine may undershoot when revved hard in neutral.
DLYTM3.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Crisper Free-Rev RPM Return**: * Lower `DLYTM3` from 255 counts (~16 seconds) down to 50 to 80 counts (~3 to 5 seconds) to eliminate excessive idle hang after revving the engine in neutral.
* **High-RPM Neutral Stall Protection**: * Ensure `DLYTM3` remains at or above 40 counts (~2.5 seconds) so aggressive camshafts have adequate time to catch descending revs.
* **Threshold Trigger**: * Only triggers when engine speed exceeds `DLYRPM` (factory ~1500 RPM) at standstill.

DLYRPM.overview: DLYRPM defines the engine speed threshold that switches the stationary closed-throttle dashpot delay between the standard low-RPM timer DLYTIM2 and the extended high-RPM timer DLYTM3. When the accelerator pedal is released at a standstill, the severity of the deceleration depends heavily on engine speed. If the engine was merely idling or gently revved below DLYRPM, a brief dashpot delay (DLYTIM2) is sufficient to catch the engine smoothly. However, if the engine was revved to high RPM above DLYRPM, the extended dashpot delay (DLYTM3) is required to ensure safe recovery. In factory calibrations, DLYRPM is set to 94 counts, corresponding to an engine speed threshold of approximately 1504 RPM (nominally 1500 RPM).

MPHREF.overview: MPHREF defines the critical vehicle speed threshold that separates moving or rolling deceleration logic from stationary closed-throttle idle control. When a vehicle is moving down the road at highway or suburban speeds, letting off the accelerator pedal requires vehicle deceleration dashpot airflow to cushion engine braking. Conversely, when the vehicle comes to a complete standstill, the engine controller must transition into true stationary idle speed regulation to maintain target idle RPM without causing vehicle creeping or engine surging. MPHREF establishes this vehicle speed boundary across multiple engine control routines, incorporating approximately 1.5 mph of built-in hysteresis to prevent rapid cycling around the switch point. In factory calibrations, MPHREF is set to 8 counts, corresponding to a vehicle speed threshold of 4.0 mph.

On manual transmission cars with lightweight flywheels, keeping MPHREF around 4 to 5 mph ensures that coasting to a stop sign keeps the dashpot active until the vehicle has almost completely stopped, preventing stall dips. Do not raise MPHREF above 10 mph, as stationary idle feedback will engage while coasting at road speeds, reducing engine vacuum braking.

* **Speed Threshold Limits**: * Avoid raising `MPHREF` above 10.0 mph to prevent unwanted idle hunting while coasting down hills.

PNDLT.overview: PNDLT defines the engine speed error deadband threshold required before the controller triggers the automatic transmission Park/Neutral to Drive kick opening table. When the driver shifts an automatic transmission from Park or Neutral into Drive or Reverse, the transmission hydraulic clutches engage and the torque converter impeller suddenly loads the crankshaft. To prevent the resulting mechanical drag from causing a severe engine stumble or stall, the ECU monitors the RPM drop. If the difference between actual engine speed and target idle speed exceeds PNDLT, the controller advances its memory pointer to index the PNDRK opening step table. In factory calibrations, PNDLT is configured to 400 counts, representing an RPM delta trigger threshold of approximately 200 RPM.

PNDLT.tuners_guide: PNDLT controls how quickly the ECU intervenes when shifting into gear. For loose, high-stall aftermarket torque converters that produce very little idle drag, PNDLT can be raised to prevent premature step kicks.

* **Threshold Minimum**: * Do not lower `PNDLT` below 50 RPM to avoid false triggering from natural idle lope.

PNDRK.overview: PNDRK is a 2D calibration curve that establishes the pre-emptive opening steps added to the idle air stepper motor when shifting an automatic transmission from Park or Neutral into Drive. When the transmission shifts into gear, the hydraulic torque converter immediately places a heavy mechanical drag on the crankshaft. If the engine controller relied purely on closed-loop feedback to catch this load, engine speed would sag significantly before the stepper motor could respond. PNDRK injects a rapid, pre-emptive kick opening into the stepper motor as a function of coolant temperature. In factory calibrations, PNDRK commands a large opening kick during cold warm-up (approximately 20 to 25 steps) that tapers down to 4 to 6 steps once the engine and transmission fluid are fully warmed up.

PNDLTP.overview: PNDLTP defines the engine speed error threshold required before the controller triggers the automatic transmission Drive to Park/Neutral step reduction table. When the driver shifts an automatic transmission out of Drive or Reverse into Park or Neutral, the hydraulic load of the torque converter is suddenly released from the crankshaft. If the idle air stepper motor remained in its loaded in-gear position, the sudden uncoupling of transmission drag would cause the engine to flare upward loudly into a high-RPM surge. To prevent this flare, the ECU detects the RPM change upon shifting out of gear. If the difference between target idle speed and actual engine speed exceeds PNDLTP, the controller advances its memory pointer to index the DRPNK closing step table. In factory calibrations, PNDLTP is set to 160 counts, representing an RPM delta trigger threshold of approximately 80 RPM.

DRPNK.overview: DRPNK is a 2D calibration curve that establishes the closing step reduction applied to the idle air stepper motor when shifting an automatic transmission from Drive into Park or Neutral. While in gear, the idle air motor is held open further to overcome the hydraulic viscous drag of the torque converter. When the driver shifts into Park or Neutral, this converter load vanishes instantly. If the extra in-gear airflow were not removed immediately, the unloaded engine would flare to high RPM. DRPNK commands an instantaneous reduction in stepper motor opening steps as a function of engine coolant temperature. In factory calibrations, DRPNK commands a large step reduction during cold warm-up (approximately 15 to 20 steps) that tapers down to 6 to 8 steps when the engine is fully warmed up.

ACOFFK.overview: ACOFFK defines the closed-throttle stepper motor kick step reduction applied when the air conditioning compressor clutch disengages. While the air conditioning compressor is pumping, auxiliary bypass airflow is injected to prevent the engine from stalling under compressor load. When the air conditioning thermostat satisfied signal opens and the magnetic clutch disengages, this compressor pumping load drops instantly to zero. If the auxiliary air were left in the intake manifold, the suddenly unloaded engine would flare upward into an annoying high-RPM idle surge. ACOFFK immediately subtracts a calibrated block of steps from the idle stepper motor to neutralize the load drop and prevent idle flaring. In factory calibrations, ACOFFK is set to 8 counts, commanding an immediate 8-step closure upon compressor disengagement.

However, if ACOFFK is set too high, the motor will close too far, causing the engine to dip below target idle and stumble when the A/C turns off. * **Cycling Equilibrium**: * Balance `ACOFFK` against `AC2KCK` to make compressor cycling completely transparent to vehicle occupants.

AC2KCK.overview: AC2KCK defines the pre-emptive opening step kick added to the idle air stepper motor when the air conditioning compressor clutch is commanded to engage. When the air conditioning system calls for cooling, the magnetic compressor clutch locks up, suddenly imposing heavy mechanical pumping drag on the engine. If the engine controller waited for engine speed to drop before reacting, closed-loop feedback would be too slow, resulting in a severe idle speed dip or stall. AC2KCK pre-emptively steps the idle air motor open at the exact instant the compressor clutch is energized. In factory calibrations, AC2KCK is set to 4 counts, injecting an immediate 4-step opening kick to absorb the compressor engagement shock.

PERKCK.overview: PERKCK defines the scaling percentage multiplier applied to the off-idle air conditioning airflow adder ACCTBL. Depending on whether the air conditioning system is transitioning between active states or operating in steady-state off-idle cruising, the full airflow step offset looked up from ACCTBL may need to be scaled down. PERKCK acts as a global proportioning scalar applied to the raw speed-dependent steps retrieved from ACCTBL. In factory calibrations, PERKCK is set to 192 counts, representing an airflow scaling factor of exactly 75 percent (192/256).
PERKCK.overview_markdown: `PERKCK` defines the scaling percentage multiplier applied to the off-idle air conditioning airflow adder `ACCTBL`. Depending on whether the air conditioning system is transitioning between active states or operating in steady-state off-idle cruising, the full airflow step offset looked up from `ACCTBL` may need to be scaled down. PERKCK acts as a global proportioning scalar applied to the raw speed-dependent steps retrieved from `ACCTBL`. In factory calibrations, `PERKCK` is set to 192 counts, representing an airflow scaling factor of exactly 75 percent (192/256).
PERKCK.tuners_guide: PERKCK provides a simple master scalar to increase or decrease off-idle air conditioning airflow across all vehicle speeds without modifying the individual points in ACCTBL. If your vehicle needs slightly more decel dashpot air with the A/C running across the entire speed spectrum, raising PERKCK from 192 (75%) up to 230 or 255 (90% to 100%) scales up the entire curve proportionally. Conversely, if off-idle A/C airflow is generally too generous across all cruising speeds, lowering PERKCK to 128 (50%) reduces total A/C dashpot air proportionally.
PERKCK.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Global Scaling of ACCTBL**: * Adjust `PERKCK` to scale overall off-idle A/C airflow up or down without reshaping the individual speed breakpoints in `ACCTBL`.
* **Increasing Dashpot Air**: * Raise `PERKCK` to 220 to 255 counts (86% to 100%) to provide stronger overall anti-stall dashpot air with the A/C on.
* **Linear Percentage Multiplier**: * 255 counts represents 100% full scale; factory setting of 192 counts represents 75%.

Takes effect at closed throttle idle to regulate AcClutchAisAdjustmentConstant.

AC4KCK.overview: AC4KCK defines the secondary stepper motor opening kick offset applied before air conditioning clutch engagement under elevated intake manifold pressure conditions. If the engine is operating under higher manifold pressure (above the safety vacuum lockout threshold DCLMN2) when the A/C clutch engagement sequence begins, intake manifold density is already elevated. Under these conditions, applying the standard sea-level kick opening would introduce too much air, causing an unwanted idle surge. AC4KCK supplies a signed corrective offset that fine-tunes the pre-engagement stepper position for elevated manifold pressure conditions. In factory calibrations, AC4KCK is set to 250 counts, representing a signed negative trim of -6 steps.

Under these conditions, applying the standard sea-level kick opening would introduce too much air, causing an unwanted idle surge. `AC4KCK` supplies a signed corrective offset that fine-tunes the pre-engagement stepper position for elevated manifold pressure conditions. In factory calibrations, `AC4KCK` is set to 250 counts, representing a signed negative trim of -6 steps.
AC4KCK.tuners_guide: AC4KCK fine-tunes A/C clutch engagement behavior under elevated manifold pressure. In standard street applications, this parameter rarely requires modification. If the vehicle surges upward when the A/C compressor engages while idling in gear with high manifold absolute pressure (such as with an aggressive camshaft that generates low vacuum), increasing the negative magnitude of AC4KCK (for example, setting to 248 counts / -8 steps) will trim down the pre-engagement air surge. Retain factory setting (-6 steps) for standard induction setups.

* **Signed Two's Complement**: * Stored as a signed byte (250 counts = -6 steps).
* **Gated by DCLMN2**: * Only applies when manifold absolute pressure is above `DCLMN2`.
AC4KCK.operating_conditions:
Takes effect at closed throttle just before the A/C clutch engages under elevated intake manifold pressure (low vacuum), fine-tuning the pre-engagement idle air kick.

AC3KCK.overview: AC3KCK defines the secondary stepper motor opening kick offset applied after air conditioning clutch engagement under elevated intake manifold pressure conditions. Once the compressor clutch has successfully engaged, the controller evaluates intake manifold pressure. If manifold absolute pressure is above DCLMN2, indicating that the engine is already drawing adequate air mass, applying the full standard in-gear A/C step addition would over-compensate, causing engine speed to flare above target. AC3KCK applies a small signed trim offset to fine-tune the post-engagement motor position under elevated manifold pressure. In factory calibrations, AC3KCK is set to 254 counts, representing a signed trim of -2 steps.

* **Companion Pair**: * Works directly with `AC4KCK`.

ACTIM2.overview: ACTIM2 defines the secondary transition delay timer utilized during alternate air conditioning clutch engagement paths. During certain operational transitions (such as re-engaging the compressor following a part-throttle cutout or recovering from overrun), the idle air motor requires a calibrated blending delay to smoothly integrate the A/C idle air offset. ACTIM2 reloads the A/C transition timer upon entering the secondary engagement branch, ensuring that airflow transitions remain gradual and do not induce driveline shudder. In factory calibrations, ACTIM2 is set to 36 counts, providing an engagement blending window of approximately 2.25 seconds.
ACTIM2.overview_markdown: `ACTIM2` defines the secondary transition delay timer utilized during alternate air conditioning clutch engagement paths. During certain operational transitions (such as re-engaging the compressor following a part-throttle cutout or recovering from overrun), the idle air motor requires a calibrated blending delay to smoothly integrate the A/C idle air offset. `ACTIM2` reloads the A/C transition timer upon entering the secondary engagement branch, ensuring that airflow transitions remain gradual and do not induce driveline shudder. In factory calibrations, `ACTIM2` is set to 36 counts, providing an engagement blending window of approximately 2.25 seconds.
ACTIM2.tuners_guide: ACTIM2 controls transition pacing in the secondary A/C engagement branch. It functions identically to ACTIME and should mirror ACTIME's value in almost all calibrations. If the engine stumbles when re-engaging the compressor following deceleration or cutout, shortening ACTIM2 to 1.5 seconds (24 counts) brings full idle air compensation online faster. Conversely, if re-engagement causes a brief RPM flare, lengthening ACTIM2 to 3.0 seconds (48 counts) smooths out the ramp.
ACTIM2.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Mirroring ACTIME**: * Keep `ACTIM2` matched to `ACTIME` to maintain consistent transition timing across all engagement paths.
* **Smoothing Re-Engagement Shudder**: * Lengthen `ACTIM2` to 3.0 seconds if compressor re-engagement after decel produces driveline shudder.
* **Timer Operation**: * Loaded into `Timer_AisOrO2Sensor`, which decrements every loop tick.

OFFPER.overview: OFFPER defines the percentage proportion of the off-idle air conditioning airflow adder ACCTBL that is instantly retracted when the compressor clutch disengages. While driving off-idle with the air conditioner on, ACCTBL injects auxiliary bypass airflow to counteract compressor drag during coast-down. When the compressor clutch disengages, compressor drag vanishes immediately. If the full off-idle air offset were allowed to decay away slowly, the vehicle would continue to coast forward with diminished engine braking, feeling like the throttle is hanging open. OFFPER dictates what percentage of the ACCTBL airflow adder is instantly subtracted from the stepper motor position at the exact moment the clutch disengages. In factory calibrations, OFFPER is set to 192 counts, commanding an instantaneous retraction of exactly 75 percent (192/256) of the A/C airflow adder.
OFFPER.overview_markdown: `OFFPER` defines the percentage proportion of the off-idle air conditioning airflow adder `ACCTBL` that is instantly retracted when the compressor clutch disengages. When the compressor clutch disengages, compressor drag vanishes immediately. If the full off-idle air offset were allowed to decay away slowly, the vehicle would continue to coast forward with diminished engine braking, feeling like the throttle is hanging open. `OFFPER` dictates what percentage of the `ACCTBL` airflow adder is instantly subtracted from the stepper motor position at the exact moment the clutch disengages. In factory calibrations, `OFFPER` is set to 192 counts, commanding an instantaneous retraction of exactly 75 percent (192/256) of the A/C airflow adder.
OFFPER.tuners_guide: OFFPER controls deceleration feel when the air conditioning compressor turns off while coasting down from speed. If your vehicle feels like it surges forward or fails to decelerate cleanly when the A/C clutch disengages while coasting, increasing OFFPER to 220 to 255 counts (86% to 100%) will retract the entire A/C airflow adder immediately, restoring sharp engine braking. Conversely, if the vehicle jerks abruptly into harsh engine braking when the compressor disengages while coasting, lowering OFFPER to 128 counts (50%) leaves more residual air to cushion the transition. Retain factory setting (75%) for balanced drivability.
OFFPER.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Eliminating Coasting Forward Push**: * Increase `OFFPER` to 220 to 255 counts (86% to 100%) to instantly eliminate all A/C dashpot air when the clutch opens, restoring firm engine braking.
* **Softening Disengagement Jerk**: * Lower `OFFPER` to 128 counts (50%) if the car jerks backward into abrupt engine braking when the compressor disengages.
* **Percentage Scalar**: * 255 counts represents 100%; factory setting of 192 counts represents 75%.
OFFPER.operating_conditions:
Takes effect while driving off-idle with the air conditioner on, ACCTBL injects auxiliary bypass airflow to counteract compressor drag during coast-down.

AISMPH.overview: AISMPH defines the maximum vehicle speed ceiling for active rolling idle mode on manual transmission Chrysler vehicles. When coasting in neutral with the clutch disengaged, maintaining a slightly elevated rolling idle speed prevents the engine from stalling, provides vacuum assist for power brakes, and facilitates smooth rev-matching when shifting back into gear. However, above moderate driving speeds, the vehicle is coasting at highway velocity and should operate under normal deceleration dashpot rules rather than holding an elevated rolling idle target. AISMPH establishes this upper speed boundary. In factory calibrations, AISMPH is set to 0 counts (disabled in some automatic calibrations) or 16 counts (approximately 16 mph in manual variants), bounding rolling idle regulation to low-speed coasting.
AISMPH.overview_markdown: `AISMPH` defines the maximum vehicle speed ceiling for active rolling idle mode on manual transmission Chrysler vehicles. When coasting in neutral with the clutch disengaged, maintaining a slightly elevated rolling idle speed prevents the engine from stalling, provides vacuum assist for power brakes, and facilitates smooth rev-matching when shifting back into gear. However, above moderate driving speeds, the vehicle is coasting at highway velocity and should operate under normal deceleration dashpot rules rather than holding an elevated rolling idle target. `AISMPH` establishes this upper speed boundary. In factory calibrations, `AISMPH` is set to 0 counts (disabled in some automatic calibrations) or 16 counts (approximately 16 mph in manual variants), bounding rolling idle regulation to low-speed coasting.
AISMPH.tuners_guide: AISMPH controls rolling idle availability on manual transmission vehicles. If your manual transmission vehicle drops RPM too low or stalls when coasting up to stop signs or coasting in neutral down slight inclines, configuring AISMPH to 15 to 20 mph enables rolling idle mode, holding engine speed steady at target idle while rolling. If you dislike having an elevated idle while coasting and prefer the engine to drop immediately to base idle regardless of vehicle speed, set AISMPH to 0 mph to disable rolling idle mode entirely.
AISMPH.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Manual Transmission Coasting Stall Fix**: * Set `AISMPH` to 15 to 20 mph to keep rolling idle active when coasting in neutral, stabilizing power steering and brake assist.
* **Disabling Rolling Idle**: * Set `AISMPH` to 0 mph if you want engine RPM to drop immediately to base stationary idle whenever the throttle is released, regardless of road speed.
* **Manual Only**: * Bypassed on automatic transmission vehicles (`bitb #cfg_ATX` branch at line 8451).

RPMDLT.overview: RPMDLT defines the engine speed tolerance adder above target idle speed that permits entry into rolling idle mode on manual transmission vehicles. While coasting in neutral below the speed threshold set in AISMPH, the engine controller must decide whether engine speed is close enough to target idle to engage closed-loop rolling idle regulation. If actual engine speed is significantly higher than target idle (for instance, if the driver just downshifted or revved the engine), entering rolling idle mode prematurely would cause the controller to actively fight the descending revs. RPMDLT is added to target idle speed to form an upper RPM boundary. Only when actual engine speed is below this combined threshold is rolling idle mode activated. ISPDCY.overview: ISPDCY defines the RPM decrement step size subtracted from target idle speed during rolling idle decay. When a vehicle is operating in rolling idle mode, target idle speed is held at an elevated level. DECAIS.overview: DECAIS defines the loop counter bitmask that paces how frequently the target idle speed decay step ISPDCY is applied during rolling idle mode. AISLMH.overview: AISLMH defines the upper step limit offset added to baseline idle position to clamp the maximum opening of the idle stepper motor during rolling idle mode. While operating in rolling idle mode, closed-loop feedback dynamically adjusts stepper motor position to match target rolling idle speed. If an unexpected load or manifold pressure transient occurs, or if the driver coasts downhill with the throttle closed, unconstrained closed-loop feedback could drive the stepper motor open to near-maximum travel, causing the engine to flare loudly upon clutching in. AISLMH establishes a protective upper boundary: the desired motor position during rolling idle is never permitted to exceed baseline steps plus AISLMH. In factory calibrations, AISLMH is set to 32 counts, capping rolling idle opening at 32 steps above baseline.

In factory calibrations, `AISLMH` is set to 32 counts, capping rolling idle opening at 32 steps above baseline.

Conversely, if rolling idle struggles to hold target speed when heavy loads turn on while coasting (such as electric cooling fans or headlights), increasing AISLMH to 40 to 45 steps provides additional opening headroom.

* **Pairing with AISLML**: * Forms the upper boundary of the rolling idle window; balance against `AISLML` (lower floor).

AISLML.overview: AISLML defines the lower step limit offset subtracted from baseline idle position to clamp the minimum opening of the idle stepper motor during rolling idle mode. While the vehicle is rolling in neutral with closed throttle, the engine relies on auxiliary bypass airflow to avoid sudden stalling when the brakes are applied or when clutching back into gear. If the closed-loop controller observed a minor overspeed and drove the stepper motor completely shut, the engine would be left with zero bypass air, causing an immediate stall when vehicle speed halted. AISLML establishes a protective lower floor: the desired motor position during rolling idle is never permitted to drop below baseline steps minus AISLML. In factory calibrations, AISLML is set to 4 counts, ensuring the stepper motor cannot close more than 4 steps below the calibrated baseline during rolling idle.

If the closed-loop controller observed a minor overspeed and drove the stepper motor completely shut, the engine would be left with zero bypass air, causing an immediate stall when vehicle speed halted. `AISLML` establishes a protective lower floor: the desired motor position during rolling idle is never permitted to drop below baseline steps minus `AISLML`. In factory calibrations, `AISLML` is set to 4 counts, ensuring the stepper motor cannot close more than 4 steps below the calibrated baseline during rolling idle.
AISLML.tuners_guide: AISLML protects against rolling idle undershoot stalls. If your engine dips below idle and stalls when you coast to a stop in neutral or apply the brakes while rolling, ensuring that AISLML is tightly bounded (between 2 and 4 steps) prevents the closed-loop controller from over-retracting the stepper motor. If you have an aggressive camshaft that needs a high, steady baseline airflow while rolling, reducing AISLML to 2 steps (or even 0 steps) keeps the stepper motor firmly propped at or above the baseline position. Never increase AISLML above 10 steps, as this allows the motor to step down too far, risking a decel die-out.
AISLML.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Coasting Undershoot Protection**: * Keep `AISLML` between 2 and 4 steps to guarantee that the idle stepper motor cannot choke off bypass air while rolling to a stop.
* **Aggressive Camshaft Floor**: * Lower `AISLML` to 1 or 2 steps on high-overlap camshafts to ensure rolling idle never drops below the baseline airflow floor.
* **Excessive Travel Warning**: * Avoid setting `AISLML` higher than 8 steps, as the controller can pull the motor shut on rolling overspeeds, inducing stalls.

ACDTMP.overview: ACDTMP defines the engine coolant temperature threshold above which the controller is permitted to engage part-throttle air conditioning compressor cutout. Operating an air conditioner places additional thermal load on the vehicle radiator and cooling system via the condenser, as well as mechanical parasitic load on the crankshaft. If the engine begins to overheat, or if maximum acceleration is demanded under high thermal load, disengaging the compressor clutch reduces engine temperature and frees up horsepower. ACDTMP acts as a temperature gate for part-throttle A/C cutout. In factory calibrations, ACDTMP is set to 255 counts, corresponding to 260 °F. This maximum factory value effectively disables part-throttle A/C cutout on stock calibrations, leaving compressor cutout reserved primarily for wide-open throttle.

By lowering ACDTMP from 260 °F down to 215 °F or 220 °F (238 to 242 counts), the controller will automatically disengage the air conditioning compressor whenever coolant temperature exceeds that threshold during brisk part-throttle driving. This sheds 5 to 10 horsepower of mechanical drag and reduces heat rejection through the radiator core, helping the engine shed heat in stop-and-go traffic. If you want part-throttle A/C cutout to remain completely disabled as the factory intended, retain 255 counts.

ACDTHR.overview: ACDTHR defines the throttle position sensor voltage delta threshold required to activate part-throttle air conditioning compressor cutout. When accelerating moderately to merge onto a highway or pass traffic, disengaging the air conditioning compressor eliminates parasitic pumping loss and delivers maximum engine torque to the drive wheels. ACDTHR establishes the throttle opening threshold (measured relative to the base closed-throttle stop) above which the controller initiates a temporary compressor cutout. In factory calibrations, ACDTHR is set to 255 counts (5.0 Volts delta above idle stop). This maximum setting disables part-throttle cutout on factory calibrations, ensuring that the air conditioning remains active until true wide-open throttle is reached.

ACDSPD.overview: ACDSPD defines the maximum vehicle speed ceiling below which part-throttle air conditioning compressor cutout is permitted to engage. Part-throttle compressor cutout is designed primarily to improve low-speed urban acceleration from a standstill or low speeds. At higher road speeds, the engine is already producing sufficient power to accelerate the vehicle effortlessly, and cutting the compressor would compromise cabin comfort unnecessarily. ACDSPD.overview_markdown: `ACDSPD` defines the maximum vehicle speed ceiling below which part-throttle air conditioning compressor cutout is permitted to engage. Part-throttle compressor cutout is designed primarily to improve low-speed urban acceleration from a standstill or low speeds. At higher road speeds, the engine is already producing sufficient power to accelerate the vehicle effortlessly, and cutting the compressor would compromise cabin comfort unnecessarily. `ACDSPD` establishes the vehicle speed boundary: part-throttle A/C cutout can only engage if vehicle speed is below `ACDSPD`. In factory calibrations, `ACDSPD` is set to 0 counts (0 mph), keeping part-throttle cutout disabled stock.
ACDSPD.tuners_guide: ACDSPD bounds the operational speed range for part-throttle A/C cutout. If you have lowered ACDTMP and ACDTHR to enable part-throttle cutout, set ACDSPD to 35 to 45 mph (2240 to 2880 counts in the 16-bit word format). This will permit the compressor to disengage during brisk part-throttle take-offs and city street passing, while preserving uninterrupted air conditioning once the vehicle reaches steady highway cruising speeds. Retain 0 counts if you want part-throttle cutout to remain permanently inactive.
ACDSPD.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **City Take-Off Boost Ceiling**: * Set `ACDSPD` to 35 to 45 mph when enabling part-throttle cutout to limit compressor disengagement to low-speed city driving.
* **Highway Comfort Retention**: * Keeping `ACDSPD` below 50 mph ensures highway part-throttle cruising maintains steady cabin cooling.
* **16-Bit Word Resolution**: * Type 4 constant evaluated against 16-bit register `VehicleSpeed_HB`.
ACDSPD.operating_conditions:
Takes effect during part-throttle acceleration with the A/C on, ensuring the compressor is only cut out to assist vehicle acceleration below this road speed ceiling.

ACETIM.overview: ACETIM defines the maximum duration that part-throttle air conditioning compressor cutout is permitted to remain continuously active. When part-throttle A/C cutout engages during acceleration, the compressor clutch disengages to shed mechanical drag. However, if the driver continues to drive at part-throttle for an extended period (such as climbing a long mountain grade), holding the compressor off continuously would cause the cabin evaporator to warm up and blow hot, humid air. ACETIM acts as a maximum timeout limiter: once the cutout timer reaches ACETIM, the controller overrides the cutout and forces the compressor clutch to re-engage. In factory calibrations, ACETIM is set to 8 counts, enforcing a maximum cutout window of approximately 0.5 seconds.

ACERPM.overview: ACERPM defines the engine speed threshold above which part-throttle air conditioning compressor cutout is terminated, allowing the compressor clutch to re-engage. Part-throttle cutout is meant to assist low-RPM engine torque during the initial phase of acceleration. Once the engine has revved past its mid-range torque peak, engine horsepower output is plentiful and turbocharger boost is fully spooled. At higher engine speeds, compressor parasitic load represents a negligible fraction of total engine output. If engine speed rises above ACERPM while part-throttle cutout is active, the controller immediately clears the cutout timer and re-engages the compressor. In factory calibrations, ACERPM is set to 68 counts, corresponding to an engine speed threshold of 2176 RPM (nominally 2200 RPM).

ACAETH.overview: ACAETH defines the lockout delay timer that prevents the air conditioning compressor clutch from engaging immediately following an acceleration enrichment transient. When the driver steps into the throttle to accelerate, the fuel injection system delivers acceleration enrichment to prevent a lean tip-in stumble. If the air conditioning clutch were permitted to snap shut in the middle of this throttle tip-in transient, the sudden mechanical load shock would absorb engine torque, causing a perceptible hesitation or stumble. ACAETH enforces a mandatory waiting delay: whenever acceleration enrichment is active, the controller reloads the clutch restriction timer with ACAETH, keeping the compressor disengaged until fueling and combustion stabilize. In factory calibrations, ACAETH is set to 45 counts, enforcing a tip-in lockout delay of approximately 2.8 seconds.

If ACAETH is set too low (below 1.0 second), the compressor clutch can engage right as the turbocharger is spooling up, producing a noticeable dip in acceleration. Retain factory setting of 45 counts (~2.8 seconds) for smooth street drivability.

* **Timer Operation**: * Loaded into `Timer_AcClutchEngageRestrictionTimer`, which decrements every loop clock tick.

BTVAIS.overview: BTVAIS defines the minimum electrical system battery voltage required before the controller allows actuation of the automatic idle speed stepper motor. The 4-wire stepper motor actuator relies on electromagnetic coils to overcome internal friction, spring pressure, and intake manifold vacuum force to move the pintle. If battery voltage sags significantly, coil current is insufficient to overcome these mechanical forces, leading to weak torque, skipped steps, and permanent loss of motor position calibration. BTVAIS establishes a protective voltage floor: whenever battery voltage is below BTVAIS, stepper motor stepping pulses are completely inhibited. In factory calibrations, BTVAIS is set to 113 counts, corresponding to a battery voltage floor of approximately 11.3 Volts.
BTVAIS.overview_markdown: `BTVAIS` defines the minimum electrical system battery voltage required before the controller allows actuation of the automatic idle speed stepper motor. The 4-wire stepper motor actuator relies on electromagnetic coils to overcome internal friction, spring pressure, and intake manifold vacuum force to move the pintle. If battery voltage sags significantly, coil current is insufficient to overcome these mechanical forces, leading to weak torque, skipped steps, and permanent loss of motor position calibration. `BTVAIS` establishes a protective voltage floor: whenever battery voltage is below `BTVAIS`, stepper motor stepping pulses are completely inhibited. In factory calibrations, `BTVAIS` is set to 113 counts, corresponding to a battery voltage floor of approximately 11.3 Volts.
BTVAIS.tuners_guide: BTVAIS protects the idle air stepper motor from losing calibration during severe electrical system load transients. If running a lightweight racing battery or a high-draw aftermarket audio or fuel pump system that causes system voltage to dip momentarily to 11.0 Volts during hot idle, the factory 11.3 Volt threshold may temporarily freeze idle air motor corrections. In such cases, lowering BTVAIS slightly to 10.5 or 10.8 Volts (105 to 108 counts) maintains idle air control authority during heavy electrical draw. Never lower BTVAIS below 9.5 Volts, as stepper motor coils will reliably skip steps under manifold vacuum when supplied with inadequate voltage.
BTVAIS.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Lightweight Battery Dip Accommodation**: * Lower `BTVAIS` to 10.5 to 10.8 Volts if high-draw electric water pumps or fuel pumps pull system voltage below 11.3 Volts at hot idle.
* **Skipped Step Hazard**: * Do not lower `BTVAIS` below 9.5 Volts, as weak coil magnetism at low voltage causes the stepper motor to miscount steps and lose physical calibration.
* **Factory Safety Margin**: * Factory setting of 113 counts (11.3 Volts) ensures robust coil stepping torque under all factory operating conditions.
BTVAIS.operating_conditions:

AISFRQ.overview: AISFRQ defines the closed-loop feedback update period that governs how frequently the automatic idle speed stepper motor can make corrective position changes based on RPM error. Because an internal combustion engine has physical intake manifold volume and delayed torque response to airflow changes, making stepper motor adjustments too rapidly causes control loop instability, where the controller constantly overshoots and hunts around target idle. AISFRQ acts as a rate-limiting filter, requiring a minimum elapsed timer duration between successive closed-loop step corrections from FWDAIS or REVAIS. In factory calibrations, AISFRQ is set to 63 counts (or 127 counts in some variants), which enforces a settling delay of approximately 0.7 to 1.4 seconds between motor adjustments. This deliberate pacing allows the engine to respond and manifold vacuum to stabilize before the controller evaluates whether another step correction is needed.

AISFRQ acts as a rate-limiting filter, requiring a minimum elapsed timer duration between successive closed-loop step corrections from `FWDAIS` or `REVAIS`. In factory calibrations, `AISFRQ` is set to 63 counts (or 127 counts in some variants), which enforces a settling delay of approximately 0.7 to 1.4 seconds between motor adjustments. This deliberate pacing allows the engine to respond and manifold vacuum to stabilize before the controller evaluates whether another step correction is needed.
AISFRQ.tuners_guide: AISFRQ is a primary tool for eliminating persistent idle hunting and surging. If your engine develops a rhythmic idle lope or oscillation where the stepper motor constantly chases RPM up and down, increasing AISFRQ slows down the feedback loop, giving the intake manifold time to stabilize and curing the surging. Conversely, if the idle feedback feels sluggish and takes several seconds to catch an RPM dip when an accessory load turns on, lowering AISFRQ speeds up the response time. Never lower AISFRQ below 30 counts (~0.3 seconds), as the stepper motor will react faster than the engine can change speed, guaranteeing severe control loop hunting.
AISFRQ.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Curing Rhythmic Idle Surging**: * If idle speed oscillates up and down in an endless cycle, increase `AISFRQ` from 63 up to 90 to 127 counts to slow down the feedback response and allow manifold pressure to settle.
* **Sharpening Sluggish Recovery**: * If the idle air controller takes too long to recover from an accessory load drop, reduce `AISFRQ` to 45 to 50 counts to allow more frequent stepper nudges.
* **Minimum Stability Boundary**: * Do not set `AISFRQ` below 30 counts, as rapid corrections outpace engine mechanical response time, triggering severe hunting.

AISHLM.overview: AISHLM establishes the absolute high limit clamp for the maximum number of open steps that can ever be commanded on the automatic idle speed stepper motor. The Chrysler 4-wire stepper motor actuator physically drives a tapered pintle in and out of an auxiliary throttle bypass passage. If the controller were to continuously increment stepper opening steps without an upper limit, the motor mechanism could unscrew the pintle shaft from its internal worm gear drive or jam the actuator against its mechanical end stops, causing lost steps and permanent positioning calibration errors. Furthermore, beyond approximately 160 steps, the annular bypass opening around the pintle is completely unrestricted, and additional opening steps provide zero incremental airflow. AISHLM.overview_markdown: `AISHLM` establishes the absolute high limit clamp for the maximum number of open steps that can ever be commanded on the automatic idle speed stepper motor. AISHLM.tuners_guide: AISHLM should generally remain at 160 steps for factory and stock-style throttle bodies. AISFAN.overview: AISFAN defines the number of proactive stepper motor steps added to the target idle air position whenever the radiator cooling fan is commanded on while the throttle is closed. High-output electric cooling fans draw substantial electrical current upon startup, placing an immediate mechanical torque load on the engine through the alternator. Without anticipatory idle compensation, this sudden rotational drag causes engine idle speed to dip or sag before closed-loop idle feedback can react. In factory calibrations, AISFAN is set to 10 steps. When the cooling fan relay energizes at idle, the controller instantly increases the desired automatic idle speed motor position by this calibrated step amount, admitting extra bypass airflow to support engine idle speed and prevent engine RPM instability.

AISFAN.tuners_guide: Raising AISFAN provides greater airflow anticipation for heavy-duty aftermarket cooling fans or high-output alternators that induce a noticeable idle RPM dip when the cooling fan engages. For example, upgrading to a high-cfm electric fan drawing 25 to 30 amperes often benefits from increasing AISFAN to 15 or 20 steps to maintain seamless idle stability. Lowering AISFAN reduces the airflow kick, which is helpful if the engine noticeably flares upward in engine speed or surges whenever the fan engages. Setting AISFAN to zero disables the proactive kick entirely, forcing the controller to rely solely on reactionary proportional-integral idle speed tracking, which often leads to momentary idle speed dips.

* **Preventing Idle Flares**: * If the engine flares or surges upward when the fan turns on, lower `AISFAN` toward 4 to 6 steps.
* **Zeroing & Edge Cases**: * Setting `AISFAN` to 0 disables proactive idle feedforward, causing noticeable RPM dips before closed-loop idle recovers.

CALPOS.overview: CALPOS defines the calibrated nominal step position where the electronic controller assumes the idle air stepper motor sits during normal warm closed-throttle idle. Because stepper motors operate without a physical position feedback potentiometer, the ECU tracks motor position by counting step pulses sent to the motor coils. During closed-throttle stationary idle, adaptive routines periodically nudge motor position toward CALPOS to maintain optimal dynamic control range. Additionally, CALPOS serves as the fundamental baseline offset added to startup positioning curves and cold idle tables. In factory calibrations, CALPOS is set to 26 counts, representing 26 open steps from the fully seated pintle position on a stock throttle body.

CALPOS.tuners_guide: CALPOS must be adjusted whenever the mechanical throttle body is modified or replaced. If an aftermarket 52mm or 58mm throttle body is installed, or if the mechanical minimum air stop screw is turned inward to admit more bypass air for an aggressive camshaft, the engine will require fewer stepper motor steps to idle at target RPM. If CALPOS remains at 26 steps while the engine only needs 10 steps to idle, the adaptive routines will constantly fight to pull the motor closed. Monitor live datalogging of idle steps on a fully warmed engine; if the motor sits at 12 steps, set CALPOS to 12. Setting CALPOS to reflect true warmed-up idle steps ensures maximum dynamic opening authority during sudden load changes.
CALPOS.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Aftermarket Throttle Bodies**: * Big-bore throttle bodies allow more air leakage; adjust `CALPOS` down to 10 to 18 steps to match the lower step counts observed in live datalogs.
* **Mechanical Stop Screw Adjustment**: * If you turn the base idle stop screw inward to provide more base air for a race camshaft, reduce `CALPOS` correspondingly to keep adaptive trim centered.
* **Centering Adaptive Trim**: * Setting `CALPOS` accurately gives the idle stepper motor equal dynamic range to step open or closed when loads change.
CALPOS.operating_conditions:

CALRAT.overview: CALRAT defines the loop counter bitmask that paces how frequently the engine controller nudges the automatic idle speed stepper motor toward its nominal idle position. When the engine is idling at steady state with engine speed within a narrow window around target idle, the ECU gradually converges the stepper motor toward the calibrated baseline step position set in CALPOS. To prevent this centering action from causing perceptible idle speed fluctuations or fighting closed-loop proportional corrections, updates must occur very slowly. CALRAT masks the main program loop counter to enforce a deliberate update interval. In factory calibrations, CALRAT is configured to 7 counts, which functions as a binary bitmask allowing an adjustment only once every 8 main loop cycles, or approximately every 88 milliseconds.

BSTSWS.overview: BSTSWS defines the digital input pin bitmask on the switch input port used by the engine controller to read a driver-operated dual-boost selection switch. When switchable boost is enabled in the calibration option registers, the controller tests this bit against the hardware switch register during every main program loop pass. If the switch state indicates that low-boost mode is selected, the controller overrides the primary engine-speed boost target curve with the low-boost ceiling constant. This mechanism allows the driver to alternate between high-power boost and conservative low-boost settings on the fly for varying weather, traction, or fuel availability.

WSGRPM.overview: WSGRPM defines the primary wide-open throttle turbocharger boost target curve as a function of engine speed. The engine controller uses this table to establish the baseline gauge boost ceiling across the entire operating rev range. Factory calibrations typically establish a conservative mid-range boost plateau of approximately 9 to 11 psi of boost above atmospheric pressure, gently tapering the target at high engine speeds to prevent excessive exhaust backpressure and keep the turbocharger within its peak compressor efficiency island. This table acts as the foundational boost ceiling that all secondary safety tables compare against.

The engine controller uses this table to establish the baseline gauge boost ceiling across the entire operating rev range. Factory calibrations typically establish a conservative mid-range boost plateau of approximately 9 to 11 psi of boost above atmospheric pressure, gently tapering the target at high engine speeds to prevent excessive exhaust backpressure and keep the turbocharger within its peak compressor efficiency island. WSGRPM.tuners_guide: Raising this table increases maximum engine boost and torque output across the entire RPM curve. When tuning modified engines with upgraded intercoolers and high-octane fuel, tuners typically elevate this curve to 14 to 18 psi on 2-bar sensors, or up to 25 to 30 psi on 3-bar MAP sensors. Because the boost target selection logic uses a strict minimum-wins comparison across all six boost tables, any table with a lower value will override WSGRPM. Therefore, when raising WSGRPM, verify that the companion tables for boost ramp time, coolant temperature, charge temperature, vehicle speed, and part throttle are adjusted accordingly. Setting values higher than the turbocharger can physically produce will cause the wastegate duty cycle to saturate at 100 percent.
WSGRPM.tuners_guide_markdown:
* **Primary Boost Ceiling Adjustment**: * Elevating points raises the peak boost target across the RPM range for increased engine power. * Common performance targets range from 14 to 18 psi on factory 2-bar MAP sensors, and 20 to 30 psi on 3-bar sensors.
* **Minimum-Wins Target Hierarchy**: * The ECU evaluates six tables sequentially (`WSGRPM`, `WSGTIM`, `WSGCLT`, `WSGCHG`, `MXSBST`, `WSGPRT`) and selects the smallest value. * Companion limit tables must be raised alongside `WSGRPM` to prevent unexpected boost capping.
* **3-Bar MAP Sensor Rescaling**: * Converting to a 3-bar sensor doubles the pressure span per count, requiring complete table rescale to maintain intended boost targets.
* **Turbine Flow Considerations**: * Tapering boost targets slightly above 5200 RPM helps prevent severe exhaust manifold backpressure on small turbine housings.

STGBST.overview: STGBST defines the maximum allowable turbocharger boost pressure permitted while launch control staging mode is actively engaged. When the staging logic is triggered by clutch or brake engagement at a standstill, the engine controller applies specialized spark cut and fuel rev limiting while restricting manifold pressure to this threshold. In factory Turbonator calibrations, STGBST is calibrated to 41 counts, corresponding to approximately 4.7 psi of boost above atmospheric pressure. Holding boost to this calibrated ceiling prevents excessive wheel spin on launch while spooling the turbocharger to build immediate torque at the starting line.

WSGTIM.overview: WSGTIM governs the rate at which turbocharger boost is permitted to ramp upward over time once wide-open throttle is applied. The engine controller monitors an internal boost timer that increments while the engine is producing power above minimum tracking RPM. By looking up allowed boost as a function of elapsed timer counts, the controller prevents instantaneous boost spikes and delivers a progressive, predictable torque onset. Factory calibrations use this table to smooth powertrain shock loads on front-wheel-drive transaxles and prevent sudden tire spin when the throttle snaps open.
